title: A Zelda Secret Room Is Named After a Magazine Contest Winner
hook:
In 1990 a Nintendo Power reader named Chris Houlihan won a contest, and Nintendo hid his name in a secret rupee room in A Link to the Past. It took 33 years to learn who he was. Have you ever landed in the Chris Houlihan room?
Gameplay is from Shards of Irsa, a game I'm making.
script: Did you know a secret room in A Link to the Past is named after a magazine contest winner? In 1990, Nintendo Power ran a contest that asked readers to photograph themselves with a Final Fantasy enemy called Warmech. The prize was having your name placed inside an upcoming Nintendo game. The winner was Chris Houlihan. When A Link to the Past reached America in April 1992, his name was hidden inside it. Deep in the game there is a room filled with rupees. A tile inside reads, my name is Chris Houlihan, this is my top secret room.The room is a fail-safe. When the game cannot work out where Link is supposed to be, it sends him there. Players found ways to trigger it on purpose, and the hunt for the real Chris Houlihan became a mystery that lasted more than thirty years. Then, in September 2025, a YouTuber named Kevin Hainline said he had met him by chance through his own mother. He shared a letter from a Nintendo Power editor explaining the prize. Houlihan's father had entered the contest in his son's name. The man himself was reportedly not that excited about it. Have you ever landed in the Chris Houlihan room? Follow for more gaming history.
